subject: general
question: When the MP is positive but declining, it means __________

options.text: TP increases at a constant rate
TP increases at a decreasing rate
TP increases at an increasing rate

solution:
The correct answer is __**TP increases at a decreasing rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **When Marginal Product (MP) is positive but declining, Total Product (TP) continues to increase but at a decreasing rate.**
 
• This indicates that each additional unit of input contributes less to the total output than the previous unit.
 
• The phenomenon is often observed in the phase of diminishing returns in production processes.
 
• It reflects the point where the efficiency of additional inputs starts to fall, though they still contribute positively to the overall output.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal Product (MP):**

 
 
• Marginal Product is the additional output produced by adding one more unit of a specific input, keeping other inputs constant.
 
• It is a key concept in the study of production and efficiency in economics.
 
• When MP is positive but declining, it suggests diminishing marginal returns.
 
 
 
• **Total Product (TP):**
 
 
• Total Product represents the total quantity of output produced with a given quantity of inputs.
 
• It is a cumulative measure of the production process efficiency.
 
• TP increases initially at an increasing rate, then at a decreasing rate, and eventually may decline.
 
 
 
• **Diminishing Returns:**
 
 
• The law of diminishing returns states that as more of a variable input is added to a fixed input, the additional output produced from each additional unit of the variable input eventually decreases.
 
• This principle is crucial in resource allocation and production planning.
 
 
 
• **Production Function:**
 
 
• A production function illustrates the relationship between inputs used in production and the resulting output.
 
• It helps in understanding the efficiency and productivity of different input combinations.
